samples.scenario: Attacker inside a segmented VLAN launches ARP spoofing to hijack DNS traffic between a DNS server and client machines to redirect queries to malicious IPs.

technical_data.arp_spoof_packet_capture:
Frame 12: 60 bytes on wire (480 bits), 60 bytes captured
Ethernet II, Src: 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e, Dst: ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff (Broadcast)
Address Resolution Protocol (reply)
    Opcode: Reply (2)
    Sender MAC address: 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e
    Sender IP address: 10.10.10.1
    Target MAC address: 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:6f
    Target IP address: 10.10.10.50

--- Explanation ---
Attacker MAC 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e sends unsolicited ARP replies claiming to be DNS server 10.10.10.1 to victim 10.10.10.50, poisoning its cache.
technical_data.switch_log_snippet:
Timestamp: 2024-06-01T14:12:30Z
Interface Gig2/0/12 MAC 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e ARP IP 10.10.10.1
Dynamic ARP Inspection violation detected - ARP spoofing suspected
Packet dropped.
technical_data.network_traffic_anomaly: Multiple unsolicited ARP replies claiming DNS server IP from attacker MAC observed every 15 seconds.
technical_data.mitigation_commands:
On Cisco switch:
switch(config)# ip arp inspection vlan 20
switch(config)# arp access-list dns_spoof_acl
switch(config-arp-acl)# permit ip host 10.10.10.1 mac 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:01
switch(config-arp-acl)# exit
switch(config)# ip arp inspection filter dns_spoof_acl vlan 20

indicators: Unsolicited ARP replies claiming DNS server IP from attacker MAC
Client ARP cache shows DNS server IP mapped to attacker MAC
Switch DAI logs indicate ARP inspection violation on attacker port
Repeated unsolicited ARP reply packets without requests
samples.detection_method: Enable Dynamic ARP Inspection on VLAN 20 to validate ARP packets; monitor switch logs for ARP violations; analyze network traffic for frequent unsolicited ARP replies; use client-side ARP cache monitoring tools to detect suspicious MAC-IP mappings.
